newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Swedish '97 new car registrations 200,000.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swedish '97 new car registrations 200,000.

text.p: Swedish car industry organisation, the Association of Swedish Automobile Manufacturers and Wholesalers, said on Monday it had raised its forecast for 1997 new car registrations to 200,000 from 190,000.

Kurt Palmgren, managing director of Bilindustriforeningen, said new Swedish rules about company cars, a general improvement on car prices, expectations of a rise in private consumption and lower interest rates were behind the change in the forecast.
"Our 30 percent increase in the monthly figure for January corresponds quite well with our new year forecast of 200,000 if the figures are seasonally adjusted," he told Reuters.

"We should see a reaction from the company car side in the first half of the year. Last year the company car market was dead and if there is pent up demand, it should materialise in the first half of the year," Palmgren said.
Some say that the new company car rules may tempt people to buy smaller cars.
"After only one month it is too early to say if company car buyers will switch to smaller cars," Palmgren said.
The industry organisation has announced a rise of 30 percent in new car registrations in January this year to 13,999 compared to the same month a year ago.
